scene: At the Deer Park near Bārāṇasī, the Buddha asks five monks about five categories of experience.
question: Is any of these five changing parts of experience fit to call 'mine,' 'I am this,' or 'my self'?
main_point: Each of the five can cause trouble, changes over time, and does not obey your wishes. So the text says none is fit to call 'mine,' 'I am this,' or 'my self.' It connects seeing this clearly with release.
reading_cue: The text repeats the same argument for all five. Use the first one to learn the pattern. Later, watch for the repeated line: 'This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.'
not_saying: This passage is not trying to prove that nobody exists. It asks whether these five changing parts of experience are fit to call 'mine,' 'I am this,' or 'my self.'
